senses.gloss: दिश् [cf. Z. dis; Gk. δείκνυμι; Lat. dīco, in-dĭcare &c.; Goth. teihan; O. E. téon (fr. tíhan).]

quarter, region, direction, place, part (pl., rarely sg. the whole world, e.g. दिशि दिशि, in all directions, everywhere, Bhartṛ. i, 86; दिग्भ्यस्, from every q˚, BhP. i, 15, 8 ; दिशो दिशस्, hither and thither, Pañc. ii, 116/117; दिशोऽवलोक्य, looking into the q˚ of the sky i.e. into the air, Ratn. iv, 4/5 दि॑शो ऽन्तात्, from the extremities of the world, ib., Introd. 6)
country, esp. foreign country, abroad (cf. दिग्-आगत and -लाभ, below)
space (beside काल), Kap. ii, 12
the numeral 10 (cf. above), Śrutab.; Sūryas.
a hint, reference, instance, example, Suśr.; Sāh., Sch.; precept, order, manner, RV.
दिश् [cf. δίκη O. H. G. zeiga (see also दिशा)];
mark of a bite, L.
N. of a river, MBh. vi, 327.
3. दिश् a vulgar form for दृश्, to see, Pāṇ. i, 3, 1, Vārtt. 13, Pat.
दिशो = दिशस् (gen. of 2. दिश्) in comp.
दिशो—दण्ड m. ‘sky-staff’, a partic. appearance in the sky.
दिशो—दाह m. = दिग्-, Divyāv.
दिशो—भाग w.r. for दिशो—भाज्, mfn. one who runs away in all directions, Pañc. (B) iv, 15, 114/115.
दिशो—भाग w.r. for दिशो—भाज्, mfn. one who runs away in all directions, Pañc. (B) iv, 15, 114/115.
दिशो—यायिन् mfn. spreading in all directions, Kād.
दिशम् ind. = 2. दिश्, ifc. (g. शरद्-आदि).
दिशस् f. region, quarter &c., L.
दिशा f. direction, region, quarter or point of the compass, MBh. iv, 1716 &c.; Hār. 2243 (cf. अन्तर- and अवान्तर-)
N. of the wife of Rudra-Bhīma, VP.
दिशा—गज m. = दिक्-करिन्, Hariv.; R.
दिशा—चक्षुस् m. ‘sky-vision’, N. of a son of Garuḍa, MBh. v, 3595,
दिशा—पाल m. = दिक्-, Hariv. 273
दिशान m. an instructor in sacred knowledge, L.
दि॑श्य mfn. relating to the quarters of the sky or to the horizon, being there, ĀśvGṛ.; Kauś.
relating to space, Kaṇ. ii, 2, 10
foreign, outlandish, Śiś. iii, 76
दि॑श्या f. N. of a kind of brick, ŚBr.; KātyŚr.
दिष्ट॑ mfn. shown, pointed out, appointed, assigned (दिष्टा गतिस्, ‘the appointed way’ i.e. death, R. ii, 103, 8)
fixed, settled
directed, bidden, RV.; AV.; MBh.; R. &c.
दिष्ट॑ m. time, L.
a sort of Curcuma, L.
N. of a son of Manu Vaivasvata, Pur.
दिष्ट॑ n. appointed place, ChUp. v, 9, 2
aim, goal, TBr. ii, 4, 2, 2 &c.
allotment, assignment, decree
fate, destiny, AV. x, 3, 16; MBh.
direction, order, command, BhP. v, 1, 11 &c.; Rājat. iv, 121
a description according to space and time (i.e. of a natural phenomenon), Sāh.
दिष्ट—कारिन् mfn. executing an order or acting according to fate, BhP. iv, 28, 1.
दिष्ट-गमन n. dying, death (cf. दिष्टा गतिः), HirP.
दिष्ट—दृश् mfn. looking at fate or at one's lot, BhP. iv, 21, 22.
दिष्ट—पर mfn. relying on fate, fatalist, MBh. iii, 1214.
दिष्ट—भाव m. ‘appointed state’ i.e. death, MBh. v, 4529.
दिष्ट—भुज् mfn. reaping the appointed results of one's works, BhP. vii, 13, 39.
दिष्टान्त m. ‘appointed end’ i.e. death, MBh.; R. &c.
दिष्टि f. direction, prescription, TāṇḍyaBr. xxv, 18
auspicious juncture, good fortune, happiness (esp. instr. ˚ट्या, thank heaven! I congratulate you on your good luck! often with वर्धसे, you are fortunate), MBh.; Kāv. &c.
a kind of measure of length, Kauś., Sch. on KātyŚr.
दिष्टि—वृद्धि f. congratulation, Kād.; Hcar.
दिष्णु mfn. = देष्णु liberal.
